messages:
luisa: flagging a weird spike in attach latency hitting me-south1 GPU provisioning. Lots of small jobs timing out when mounting local nvme.
dan: any host-level telemetry?
ops-bot: [ALERT] me-south1-nodegroup-21: nvme io_wait 95th=420ms; read_errors +5 in 15m.
tess: I see scrub-run overlap on that nodegroup; janitor concurrency was bumped to 16 for scale tests last night.
luisa: timeline: 1751234400 scrub window started -> 1751234450 provisioning surge -> attach timeouts start at 1751234460.
dan: mitigation: temporarily pause scrub on nodegroup-21 and drain non-critical GPU attach queues.
luisa: applying pausing patch: 
```
kubectl -n infra patch configmap janitor-config --type merge -p '{"data":{"scrub_enabled":"false","scrub_override_groups":"nodegroup-21"}}'
```
ops-bot: [INFO] scrub_disabled for nodegroup-21 by luisa at 1751234570.
tess: also labeling the cohort to avoid new batch onboards: `kubectl label nodes -l cohort=nodegroup-21 no-new-onboard=true`
dan: moving high-priority provisioning to me-south1-fallback cluster (cross-region) — note: increased reservation cost and potential inter-region egress. Finance will want numbers.
luisa: good call. Quick measurement: prior to pause avg attach latency 1.1s failure rate 6%; after pause 200s later: 0.2s and failure rate 0.5%. Queue progressing.
rb-sre: opened ticket SR-7832 to track host disk replacement + SMART ingestion. Suggest we add a nightly scrub cap of 4 workers per cohort and avoid overlapping with peak provisioning windows.
dan: long term action items: 1) ingest SMART history into telemetry, 2) scrub scheduler to prefer off-peak, 3) automated node-labeling when nvme errors spike.
tess: scheduling a retro with Janitor & Provisioner teams tomorrow to change default concurrency and add guardrails.
luisa: pinned dashboard + traces in the thread. I'll keep monitoring for 1h and then re-enable scrub with lower concurrency. :thumbsup:
